entries.title: Continuous Offset Dry Rock Ravine
entries.description: One original complete dry rocky ravine terrain module: two unequal high jagged cliff walls connect through a continuous solid gently rising dry floor around a slight offset passage, open at both ends and overhead. One closed shared-vertex rock-and-floor mesh rather than repeated loose walls or scattered rocks. The tall enclosing irregular cross-sections and new dry channel are authored as a whole; no prior stream, mine wall, cliff or failed mudbank geometry imported, hidden or recoloured. Three coherent opaque matte mineral/earth roles without textures. One terrain module, zero scenes; the two cliff sides are not separate assets. Metres, native Z up, horizontal bounds-centred ground origin. End outlines are explicit but compatibility or repetition with other modules is not claimed. Static visual terrain only, no geology, erosion, water simulation, navigability, human clearance, collision, stability, climbing or safety claim.

entries.title: Upturned Rootplate and Fallen Broken Trunk
entries.description: One original whole stylised uprooted tree remnant: a tall irregular near-vertical root-and-soil plate at the thick basal end of a long leaning fallen broken trunk. A single continuous shared-vertex wood body joins the trunk to six unequal tapering exposed root arms across the plate, not detached decorative sticks. A separate closed crumbled soil plate has a finite ground sole and a real volumetric attachment with the wood hub. Dark fibrous bark, shaded bark, exposed pale broken end and matte soil use four opaque untextured PBR roles. Two editable complete meshes, one prop, zero scenes. No existing standing stump, Y-log or mangrove vertices are imported or merely rotated. Metres, native Z up, horizontal bounds-centred ground origin. Static woodland dressing only; no botanical species, root biology, storm simulation, growth, stability, physics, collision or navigation claim.

entries.title: Windthrow and Fern Understory Gap
entries.description: One static woodland windthrow and understory-gap scene, zero new reusable models. Four entire qualified existing assets retain the complete upright low-fork canopy tree, uprooted rootplate-and-fallen-trunk, mature pinnate fern and compact emerging coiled fern crown. One low scene-only forest-earth floor supports all complete original ground interfaces. The fallen remnant is the central low barrier, standing canopy stays behind it, and two different whole understory forms flank a reserved clear foreground gap; no man-made soil-road modules or extra repeated trees. All original evaluated world geometry, complete oriented triangles and per-face opaque PBR remain unchanged at unit scale. Original hierarchy/normals are explicitly baked/recomputed. This is a visual habitat composition, not a measured regeneration process, ecological claim, collision/navigation, walkability or safety certification. One scene, zero new model count.

entries.title: Open Entry and Parked Excavator Bay
entries.description: One static construction entrance and parked-machine bay. Two complete original road barricades define a wide central gap at the front edge; the complete compact tracked excavator remains parked behind the left boundary with its original fixed arm and open bucket pose. The whole low caged work light sits separately behind the right boundary. A single scene-only paved pad and contrasting central entry band organize the forecourt. Four complete instances of three old models remain at unit scale and unchanged pose, preserving every mesh, directed triangle, original node transform, normal buffer and per-face PBR. This original construction enclosure-entrance scene is distinct from the earlier scaffold/barrow worksite and mixer preparation bay. One scene, zero new models. The barricades do not close a secure perimeter; no people, traffic, active lighting, excavation, hydraulics, access compliance, construction procedure or operational safety is claimed.

entries.title: Separated Scaffold Corner Layout
entries.description: One static scaffold-corner layout scene using the complete continuous concave-L corner and two whole independently guarded straight modules at original unit scale, one rotated exactly ninety degrees. Their original nominal ten-millimetre deck gaps and every obstructing end guard remain. They are separated display units, not a connected accessible walkway. A single low scene-only ground supports all original complete finite feet; the open inner corner and front approach remain empty. All original meshes, full directed triangles, internal transforms, normal buffers and per-face opaque PBR materials remain intact. This is the original scaffold scene program, distinct from the older single scaffold with wheelbarrow and the mixer preparation bay. One scene, zero new independent models; two unique reused models and three complete instances. No climbing, passage, installation compatibility, load, stability, fall protection, construction use or safety claim.

entries.title: Continuous Four-Slope Hip Roof Shell
entries.description: One newly authored complete static four-slope hipped roof module. Two long trapezoidal roof planes meet a finite central ridge; two triangular end hips meet the same ridge endpoints and all four outer eave corners. One continuous closed 120mm vertically thick shell has a matching four-plane underside and an entirely unfilled underside opening, not a solid roof-shaped block or a gabled repeat with end walls. Four continuous fascia edges at local Z=0 mounting datum. Clay exterior, darker fascia and timber-toned underside are face materials on the same solid, without overlay planes. Unlike the existing two-slope clay repeat, porch cottage, gabled shop house or L-turn passage, both short ends are pitched roof planes and the ridge terminates inside the rectangle. One modular model, zero scenes. Static appearance only; no host house, canonical dimensional fit, structural support, weatherproofing, roof installation, drainage or building-safety guarantee. Preview floor excluded.

entries.title: Open Loading Gambrel Half-Loft Storehouse
entries.description: One newly authored complete open-loading village storehouse shell. Four-pitch gambrel roof, full side and rear enclosure, ground slab and rear half-depth elevated timber loft form a double-height front bay with a distinct open upper loading front. The front is permanently open by design, not a preview cutaway; no roof or wall is hidden in export. Side wall upper edges meet the actual inclined underside and the rear wall follows the whole folded roof profile. The full ground opening and upper loading aperture are separated by a front timber header, with the rear loft visibly set back. Nine closed editable solids, three opaque constant PBR materials, native metres. One new architecture model, zero assembled scenes. Unlike the prior single-floor assembled storehouse or full-storey shop-house, this is a different whole gambrel/half-loft spatial shell, not additional copies of old wall modules. No access stairs, cargo, door leaves, physics, manufacture, loading capacity, building-code compliance, compatible host or safety assurance.

entries.title: Integral Half-Turn Landing Stair
entries.description: One newly authored continuous static half-turn stone stair module. Six rectangular treads ascend one straight flight to a full-width rectangular intermediate landing; a second parallel straight flight reverses direction and rises through six more rectangular treads to the upper terminal. The landing crosses a real open-front central slot, connecting the two flights as one closed grounded stone mass with no internal duplicate cells, floating treads or overlaid riser pieces. This differs from existing annular90/270degree winder stairs, which turn on radial wedge treads without a full reversing landing, and from the single-flight boarding stair cart. One modular model, zero scenes. Stone body and full upward treads/platform use two opaque constant PBR face materials. Native metres, horizontal-bounds-centred ground datum. No building, rails, passengers, copied steps or site scenery. Static illustrative geometry only; no pedestrian suitability, code compliance, accessibility, railing protection, actual load, host fit, installation or safety claim.

entries.title: Level Return Foundation With Stepped Underside
entries.description: One newly authored continuous L-return village foundation module. Its entire upper wall seat stays level at1.4m while the underside rises through three distinct complete footing levels0/0.4/0.8m along the long arm and turns into the highest perpendicular return. This is a stepped underside for a rising-site visual interface, not walking stairs: there are no ascending top treads. A single connected closed solid joins all transitions and the corner, with two opaque PBR face materials distinguishing the continuous upper seat from stone sides. The original flat square foundation tile has neither this rising underside nor the integral right-angle return. Native metres, ground datum at the lowest footing and XYbounds centre. One model, zero scenes. No terrain, wall, automatic terrain fit, structural engineering, drainage, soil interaction, construction, load or safety guarantee. Only the lowest footing contacts the preview plane; the higher footings intentionally remain raised because the intended slope host is not included.

entries.title: Four-Sided Splayed Window Wall
entries.description: One newly authored complete static thick masonry wall module with an unglazed four-sided splayed through-window. The broad room-side rectangle continuously narrows along the wall depth to a smaller exterior rectangle through full left/right sloped jambs, sloped head and sloped sill. Both mouths and the entire taper between them are genuinely empty. One closed connected wall ring, no inserted opaque window, crossbar, copied frame, overlapping lintel boxes or separate sill. Unlike existing constant-section open window walls, this aperture changes both width and height through its depth, not merely wall thickness or color. One modular model, zero scenes. Two opaque constant PBR face materials distinguish masonry from cut reveals. Native metres, bounds-centred ground datum. Static illustrative geometry only; no lighting-performance, defensive use, canonical building interface, structural load, installation or safety guarantee. Preview floor excluded.

entries.title: Static Split Half Door and Frame
entries.description: One newly authored complete static horizontally split village door assembly. A full U-shaped timber frame surrounds a closed lower leaf and a separately outward-resting upper leaf, each with two distinct fixed vertical hinge stations, full straps and a pull. The upper half is held at58degrees while the lower half remains across the doorway, leaving an actual upper entry aperture and a full lower boundary. These are newly authored separate upper/lower whole leaves, not a recolored single full-height door, a second side-by-side door or copied old moving parts. All components are closed editable solids and three constant opaque PBR materials; native metres and bounds-centred ground datum. One modular model, zero scenes. Only the illustrated fixed pose is provided; no animation, continuous sweep, hinge physics, compatible old host, actual animal/child containment, lock security, manufacture, load or safety guarantee. No building or scenery; preview floor excluded.

entries.title: Fixed Open-Ring Robot Service Positioner
entries.description: One original complete empty fixed robot-service fixture appearance. A full flat-ground chamfered plinth carries two separate tapered bearing columns. Two opposed horizontal trunnion bodies support one thick octagonal through receiver in a fixed inclined pose. Four continuous stepped inward jaws meet its actual inner facets while leaving the central work opening and spaces between jaws empty. A closed side drive-case exterior meets the outside of the right column. Eleven closed editable meshes and four opaque constant untextured PBR materials. Metres, native Z up, complete horizontal bounds-centred ground origin, front -Y. All whole geometry is newly authored using generic mesh helpers only. No old service cradle, mixer drum, handwheel, display console, frame, machine or component geometry is extracted, resized, transformed or reconstructed. One complete prop, no scene or separately counted parts. No robot or workpiece is included and compatibility with existing assets is not claimed. Static art only: no rotation, tilt travel, clamping force, fit, calibration, alignment, servicing access adequacy, motion, motor or gear mechanism, electrical control, load capacity, stability, manufacture or safety claim. Positioner is a visual fixture category, not validated tooling or construction guidance.

entries.title: Fixed Circumferential-Wheel Pipe Inspection Robot
entries.description: One original complete static pipe-inspection-robot appearance. A narrow twelve-facet axial body has tapered shoulders and an integral blind forward optical recess, with a separately editable fully backed opaque lens. Two axially separated groups each carry three whole continuous radial-to-tangential dogleg arms, three short tangent-axis connectors and three complete bevel-shouldered wheels. Each wheel plane contains the long axis and its own radial direction: one upper and two lower angled wheels surround the body at each end. Real open spaces separate the body, arms and wheels, while every arm root meets a true body flat and every wheel connector meets the arm and wheel faces. Twenty closed editable meshes and four constant opaque untextured PBR roles. All whole profiles and dimensions newly authored; only generic mesh orientation/triangulation and mature export/render infrastructure reused. Not an old planar rover with extra wheels, a rescaled sampling chassis, a drone rotor or an extracted ROV capsule. One whole prop, no pipe, scene, payload or separately counted parts. Metres, native Z up, front -Y, whole horizontal bounds-centred origin and actual lower wheel edges at Z0. Static exterior game art only: no pipe diameter compatibility, centring or expansion, working joints, spring force, wheel motion, driving, traction, balance, autonomous navigation, inspection sensing, power, pressure or water resistance, load-bearing tire contact area, engineering or safety claim. Pipe inspection names the visual genre, not demonstrated operational suitability or instructions.

entries.title: Fixed Horizontal-Elbow Quill Work Robot
entries.description: One original complete fixed horizontal-elbow work-robot appearance. A grounded chamfered plinth and tall faceted pedestal support a vertical shoulder seat and one broad raised horizontal proximal casing with a chamfered upper band. A separate vertical elbow body meets a second lower horizontal forearm casing, which turns forwards in plan and includes a real through-guide near its far end. One complete long vertical quill passes with visible circumferential clearance through that guide: a lower flange seats under the case, a narrow shaft projects above to an upper stop, and a continuous lower neck ends in an integral downward-open thick cup with blind inner roof. Seven closed editable meshes, four opaque constant untextured PBR roles, metres, native Z up, front -Y and complete horizontal bounds-centred grounded origin. Every whole casing, pedestal, opening, quill and cup profile newly authored using generic mesh helpers only. Not an old vertical-plane serial robot reposed, a component extracted from a parallel robot or gantry, a desk lamp or a tool swap. One complete prop, no scene, workpiece or separately counted parts. Fixed static art only: the SCARA-like arrangement describes the visible parallel vertical axes and two horizontal casing levels, not validated kinematics, compliance, degrees of freedom, trajectory, rotation, sliding motion, guide fit, suction, grasp, force, calibration, programming, power, payload, stability, manufacture, installation or safety performance.

entries.title: Gantry-Straddled Inspection Bay
entries.description: A static robot inspection-bay composition: the complete orthogonal-rail gantry straddles the complete circumferential-wheel pipe inspector parked on the floor inside its open ground bay, while the complete empty open-ring service positioner stands outside to the right. A single scene-only slab has a distinct external front approach band. This nested overhead/ground relationship differs from the earlier four-corner service court and the parallel cargo-transfer workzone. All three original models remain whole, at unit scale and unchanged fixed pose; original buffers, internal node transforms, directed triangles and per-face materials are preserved. One scene, zero new models. The gantry tool remains clear of the inspector; the ring is empty. No lifting, holding, mechanical compatibility, inspection performance, human access compliance, workflow, operation or safety is claimed. The pipe inspector rests on the same four faceted wheel edges as its original static model, not invented finite-area soles.

entries.title: Fixed Column and Through-Guide Radial Work Arm
entries.description: One original complete fixed radial work-robot appearance. A continuous faceted ground plinth, tapered pedestal and tall narrow column include an integral lower shoulder and upper end stop. A thick annular sleeve has a genuine full bore with visible space around that column and rests on the complete lower shoulder. A separate chamfered guide over the sleeve has a real horizontal through-passage. One long straight beam runs through it with a lower seat, positive side and top space, a separate rear stop clear of the column and a continuous forward-open U end tool with two integral prongs. Six closed editable meshes and four opaque constant untextured PBR roles; metres, native Z up, front -Y and full horizontal bounds-centred ground origin. Every complete profile and dimension newly authored using generic mesh helpers only. This is not a removed gantry beam, reposed two-link elbow arm, renamed drill head, old table sleeve or end-tool-only variant. One whole prop, no workpiece, scene or independently counted parts. Static visual art only: column, sleeve, radial and guide describe visible geometry, not degrees of freedom, validated movement, trajectory, sliding or rotation, assembly path, fit, grasp, precision, actuation, load, anchoring, stability, manufacture, installation or safety performance.

entries.title: Fixed Articulated Open-Bin Carrier Robot
entries.description: One original whole fixed split-chassis transport-robot appearance. A low closed front electronics body on one axle and two ground wheels carries two complete pierced clevis plates. A continuous capped vertical pin passes with real shaft clearance through both plates and the short pierced rear-body tongue. That tongue rests on the lower clevis with a real gap below the upper plate, and connects to the full bottom of a newly authored deep open tapered bin. The complete rear bin, its separate underside frame, axle and two ground wheels form one22-degree fixed bent body relation to the front. An opaque front panel is fully backed. Fourteen closed editable meshes, four opaque constant untextured PBR materials, metres, native Z up, front -Y and complete horizontal bounds-centred ground origin. All whole shapes and dimensions are newly authored; no old rover, low platform, fork carrier, cargo-trailer tub, drawbar or eye is imported or extracted. The central captured joint and bent two-body structure are the novelty, not a deck replaced by a bin or a wheel-count variant. One empty prop, no cargo or scene. Static art only: no drive, autonomy, sensing, articulation range, steering, towing, assembly trajectory, bearing fit, load, stability, braking, manufacture, transport or equipment safety, nor compatibility with prior assets.

entries.title: Fixed Drop-Door Cavity Oven
entries.description: One original static standalone rectangular oven with a true deep front-open chamber, continuous thick five-sided housing and upper control fascia, two levels of real side shelf rails, one open wire-style grid rack and a fixed horizontal bottom-hinged thick door. The door has a recessed opaque inner panel and an underside bridge handle; two hinge barrels visibly join the door to the lower sill. Three fixed controls and four feet complete the single appliance. This is not the old solid stove box, masonry arch oven, or combined side-open toy kitchen resized. No heating, power, food safety, load, hinge motion or appliance compliance is demonstrated.
